transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alice Park (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood CSM), Maya Singh (BridgePoint Head of AI Ops), Lena Park (BridgePoint Security), Tom Reynolds (Procurement), Jared Cole (Platform)

[00:00] Alice Park: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, quick agenda — pricing update, US-West onboarding, compliance asks and next steps. i think we have about an hour.
[00:12] Maya Singh: great, thanks Alice. Tom has to step out at 17:00 local but otherwise we are good.
[00:18] Daniel Ortiz: i'll start with the tech bit — high level: us-west is available as a private region option, we can spin a private agent into your vpc or do dedicated nodes depending on the capacity commit. we ran the ballpark numbers from your current traffic and a 20% growth estimate.
[00:34] Jared Cole: question on networking — for the peering path do you require transit gateway or is a standard vpc peering sufficient? we prefer minimal networking changes.
[00:43] Daniel Ortiz: standard peering should work for the pilot; for scale we'll recommend transit gateway for cross-account routing, but for the initial week-long pilot we'll do a simple peering + route tables.
[00:58] Lena Park: security — what about audit log exports and KMS integration? our compliance team needs field-level logs, HSM-backed key control and proof of separation for the control plane.
[01:10] Priya Malhotra: we've onboarded a number of banks and can map the log export formats. we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and can integrate with HSM through your cloud provider. i'll follow up with the specific payload schemas.
[01:29] Maya Singh: timeline — we want to have the pilot in us-west before the next release window in mid-june. also, we need pricing clarity for reserved capacity vs on-demand bursts.
[01:41] Alice Park: understood. on pricing, there are two levers: a reserved tier for steady throughput and a burst overlay for peak windows. we'll send a revised doc today that shows 3 tiers plus burst pricing and a sample allocation for your traffic profile.
[02:02] Tom Reynolds: for procurement we need contract term and SLA commitments spelled out, plus a cap on overage charges during spikes.
[02:12] Alice Park: we'll include SLA language and an overage cap proposal; typically we do 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools and offer a grace buffer for known release windows.
[02:25] Maya Singh: on model compatibility — our devs run a custom quantized T5 variant, do you support custom model bundling in the private deployment?
[02:36] Daniel Ortiz: yes, the private runtime supports customer model artifacts. there are small caveats around kernel selection and quantization, we'll need to validate the model with a short onboarding run — that will be part of the baseline plan.
[02:51] Jared Cole: the baseline run — what data do you need from us? sample prompts or token distribution?
[03:01] Daniel Ortiz: sample prompt set, average and p95 sequence lengths, and a small representative dataset for latency/throughput profiling. we'll run 1: cold start latencies, 2: steady-state throughput with KV cache warm, 3: burst simulation.
[03:21] Lena Park: and for auditability we need per-request trace IDs in logs and retention for 365 days. is that supported?
[03:30] Priya Malhotra: retention is configurable for private deployments; 365 days is fine but we'll need to size storage and share the cost delta.
[03:42] Tom Reynolds: one more from procurement — who are you competing with on this deal right now?
[03:48] Alice Park: we know Anthropic and OpenAI are in the conversation for hosted endpoints; Cortex Labs was mentioned as a self-hosted alternative. our differentiation is the unified runtime + easier private onboarding and predictable economics.
[04:05] Maya Singh: do you have references in financial services who've done a similar private pilot?
[04:12] Alice Park: yes, i'll share two references — banks who've completed VPC pilots and moved to reserved capacity.
[04:20] Daniel Ortiz: technical note: for the pilot we'll configure a small dedicated pool in us-west with autoscaling disabled, and a burst overlay that can be manually activated. post-pilot we can open autoscaling or scale into a larger reserved pool.
[04:40] Jared Cole: how long to provision nodes in us-west?
[04:45] Daniel Ortiz: for dedicated nodes it's typically 2-3 business days once we have network access and service account keys; for a private VPC with strict change controls might be 5 business days.
[04:58] Maya Singh: ok, good. for the contract extension — we are looking at a 12 month extension with a 25% capacity top-up. is there an onboarding discount?
[05:09] Alice Park: yes we can offer a one-time onboarding credit and tiered discounts on the reserved commit. i'll put exact numbers in the pricing doc.
[05:22] Tom Reynolds: i have a compliance question — will Redwood give us access to the full audit trail for audit time? sometimes vendors restrict fields.
[05:31] Priya Malhotra: we provide full audit logs for private deployments, and we can deliver exports in JSON/Parquet to your S3 with role-based access.
[05:44] Maya Singh: good. next steps?
[05:47] Alice Park: recap: we will (1) send updated pricing and SLA language; (2) Daniel will send benchmark plan and schedule the baseline run; (3) Maya will send compliance questionnaire and required fields; (4) Jared will confirm network details; target pilot start is 2026-06-01.
[05:59] Tom Reynolds: thanks everyone, i'll review pricing once received.
[06:03] Alice Park: thanks folks, we'll follow up in the next 48 hours.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), timestamps approximate, some crosstalk around procurement questions.
